Competent authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against PEP lists (French, EU, UN), OFAC SDN, and domestic sanctions lists via Tracfin and other databases

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language with Latin script; no transliteration required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce within 2 months of rejection notice

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for non-operational registered office but must comply with tax residency and substance requirements for data center operations
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk for pre-incorporation stage; high for operational compliance checks post-incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for SAS incorporation plus market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration and AML compliance setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS), L.223-8 (capital deposit), R.210-1 to R.210-14 (registration formalities)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office; electronic filing via the French one-stop-shop formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) together with the M0 declaration form and supporting exhibits
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS not making a public offering; the statuts fix the share capital. A minimum of 50% of cash contributions must be deposited and blocked in escrow with a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations before filing, with the balance payable within 5 years. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers of FR_SAS, having subscribed in full to the share capital and having paid the statutory minimum fraction into escrow, adopt the statuts and establish the registered office at the address set forth therein. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [FULL_NAME] is appointed first President with the fullest powers to operate within the corporate purpose, to open bank accounts, and to represent the company before all authorities. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the filing officer is authorised to lodge the incorporation dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and to publish the required legal notice, and this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow deposit of cash share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary office or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) in France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital deposit account for the future SAS, deposit at least 50% of the cash share capital and obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage). The notary or CDC issues a release instruction immediately after the Kbis extraction is delivered.
required_dossiers: Bank transfer proof referencing the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit attestation is delayed, request written confirmation of the account reference or use a notary as an escrow agent to certify the blocked funds; re-issue the transfer with correct reference and resubmit the attestation to the preparer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of the statuts and ancillary corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French lawyer or notaire and the founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the final statuts, power of attorney for the filing officer, and the report of the contributions in kind (if any). Each shareholder signs the statuts; if notarization is sought, execute the instrument in the presence of a notary. Obtain the signed statement of no criminal disqualification (certificat de non-condamnation).
required_dossiers: In-kind contribution report and valuer's certificate (if applicable)
Power of attorney for the registration agent
Statement of compliance with French disqualification rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe queries the statuts, correct drafting errors, obtain shareholder signatures on an amendment (acte rectificatif), and refile within the 15-day cure period. If a valuer's report is missing for in-kind contributions, appoint an independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (with receipt issued by Guichet Unique)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 declaration, attach the signed statuts, capital deposit attestation, identity documents, and the domiciliation agreement for the registered office. Pay the filing fee online and receive an acknowledgement receipt with a preregistration file number. The Greffe verifies the legality of the corporate purposes and the statutory compliance.
required_dossiers: Identity documentation of the first President
Declaration of eligibility of the President
Payment proof of the registry fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit a memorandum responding to the registry's objections within 30 days through the same portal, update the statuts, and request a re-examination by the Greffe. If the objections relate to the corporate purpose, apply for a completion letter from the competent trade court or amend the corporate purpose to comply with public policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Kbis extract and completion of Article 6 post-registration formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and National Institute of Statistics (INSEE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Greffe assigns the SIREN/SIRET numbers, VAT number, and APE/NAF code; issue the Kbis extract (official registration transcript). Obtain the INPI/Guichet Unique notification of registration and store the corporate seal. The waiting period for Kbis delivery may be shortened by selecting the expedited telecopy process.
required_dossiers: Valid email address for electronic Kbis delivery
Corporate contact and operational office details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance is delayed beyond the SLA, contact the Greffe secretary directly with the preregistration file number and request the telecopy Kbis; if INSEE records are inconsistent, file a correction via the Guichet Unique and obtain an amended Kbis within the same week.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of legal notice and appointment of statutory auditors (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (legal gazette) and the Greffe for the integrated filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in a legal gazette authorised by the prefecture of the registered office, containing the company name, form, capital, address, corporate purpose, and the registry where the Kbis is issued. For SAS exceeding the legal thresholds, appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) as required by Article L.227-5 of the Code de commerce.
required_dossiers: Proof of appointment of the statutory auditor (if required)
Copy of the professional liability insurance certificate for the auditor
Payment receipt for the legal notice publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal gazette rejects the notice, correct the draft per prefecture guidelines and republish; if a statutory auditor appointment is missing, hold an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to appoint one and file the certificate with the Greffe within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), under the mission of the Inspection des Installations Classées
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploiter une Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) – data center mechanical and electromechanical EPC operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité Environnementale of the Inspection des Installations Classées (DREAL within the Ministry of Ecological Transition)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project product category: Enregistrement or Autorisation under ICPE rules. A systematic environmental impact assessment is required when the data center aggregate electrical power is ≥ 1 MW or where emergency diesel generators (ICPE 2910-B) exceed the regulatory threshold; for smaller units, an environmental registration file is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with French Order of 2 February 1998 and the European Urban Wastewater Directive (91/271/EEC) for pH, COD, BOD5, suspended solids, and total nitrogen; atmospheric emissions from diesel generators must meet EU NRMM limits (e.g., NOx ≤ 0.40 g/kWh for units between 560-1000 kW, PM ≤ 0.10 g/kWh), and coolant/refrigerant leak checks must meet Regulation (EU) 517/2014 thresholds; waste handling must follow the waste hierarchy under the French Environmental Code, with hazardous waste carrier registration for batteries and oil filters, and PFC capture for insulating gases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (avis de la commission de sécurité) covering gas suppression systems, smoke extraction, and evacuation routes; structural load inspections (certificat de solidité) by an approved bureau de contrôle for heavy IT equipment and cooling plant; workplace clearance by the DREETS/Inspection du travail for electrical installation conformity, noise exposure, and working conditions in confined mechanical zones.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — France. Professional portal: impots.gouv.fr. Mandatory business formalities portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises). Customs single window for exports: SOPRANO/DELTA (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the SAS formation dossier (statuts, registered office, manager appointments) through the Guichet unique portal, which automatically registers the entity with the RCS (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) and INSEE; INSEE issues the SIREN/SIRET identifiers. Step 2: DGFiP assigns the intra-community VAT number (FR + 11 digits or letters) upon completion of the INSEE registration; the number is published in the VIES directory. Step 3: Foreign parents without a French establishment must appoint a fiscal representative for VAT purposes (art. 289 A CGI); a non-resident contractor performing French construction works must register with the SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) of the first French construction site before commencing work. The SAS receives the extrait KBIS as proof of legal existence and tax identity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SAS is automatically subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) under art. 206 CGI. Territorial scope: profits of the French head office and attributable French permanent establishment activities are taxable in France; foreign-source profits of foreign permanent establishments are excluded under the territoriality principle. The SAS is fully taxable on profits from the French hyperscale data center EPC works.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law provides no check-the-box election; entity classification follows the statutory corporate form. Available elections: (i) small-business simplified real regime (régime réel simplifié); (ii) fiscal integration election under art. 223 A CGI where the SAS is at least 95% owned by a French-resident parent; (iii) option for group-wide worldwide profit consolidation within art. 209 quinquies CGI (where applicable); (iv) VAT group election (art. 256 C bis CGI); (v) ATAD hybrid mismatch neutralization rules (art. 212 bis CGI) apply automatically without elective designation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) — Code Général des Impôts, articles 256 to 289 C
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Statutory VAT registration is mandatory regardless of turnover for non-EU contractors performing construction works in France. For French-resident suppliers, the franchise en base de TVA (art. 293 B CGI) sets de minimis thresholds of EUR 91,900 (supply of goods) and EUR 36,800 (supply of services), with tolerance limits of EUR 101,000 and EUR 39,100; these thresholds are exceeded by the forecast hyperscale data center EPC revenue, and the SAS must therefore register for VAT with the DGFiP from its first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting under Ordonnance 2021-1190 and the Finance Act 2024 reform. Deadline: large enterprises and ETIs by 1 September 2026; SMEs/TPE by 1 September 2027. Domestic B2B invoices must be transmitted in a structured digital format (Factur-X, UBL, CII) via a certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the public portal (PPF); invoice data must be transmitted within one working day of issuance and e-reporting data within 30 days of month-end. France does not currently apply government digital stamping or per-invoice real-time clearance (unlike Italy/Hungary); compliance is monitored through the PPF, the PSTAI standard, and the mandatory reliable audit trail (piste d'audit fiable). Customs export declarations must be filed separately in the DELTA single window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of movable goods physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU (art. 262-I-1° CGI) and to services directly connected with those goods — including loading, transport, and works on movable property (art. 262-I-3° CGI). The supplier must prove that the goods left the customs territory within 90 days of transfer. For the data center EPC contract, services relating to French immovable property (installation, mechanical and electrical works on the building) are deemed supplied in France under art. 258-A CGI and remain taxable at 20%; only equipment physically installed outside France or offshore pre-commissioning engineering services performed and consumed abroad may qualify for zero-rating or a foreign place-of-supply treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: electronic Single Administrative Document (DAU) filed through DELTA/ECS, including the MRN (Movement Reference Number) and export summary declaration; the MRN must be traceable in the French and EU customs databases.

Bill of Lading / CMR / Airway Bill: commercial transport document evidencing physical departure from the EU, matching the declared exporter, consignee, value, and goods description of the customs and VAT documentation.

Inward Remittance Certificate: banking credit advice or SWIFT confirmation evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from the non-resident principal; retained with the VAT file for the statutory 6-year record retention period.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is scrutinized by the DGFiP audit services (DVNE and SIE refund desk) against customs database correlations. A missing MRN, inconsistent transport documents, or absence of payment proof within the 180-day documentary production window triggers reinstatement of 20% VAT ex officio, plus: (i) late-payment interest at 0.20% per month (art. 1727 CGI); (ii) penalties from 10% (late declaration, art. 1728 CGI) through 40% (bad-faith understatement, art. 1729 CGI) to 80% (fraudulent maneuvers, art. 1729 CGI); (iii) criminal sanctions under art. 1741 CGI, including up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years' imprisonment; (iv) joint and several liability of the main EPC contractor for VAT, penalties, and interest of its subcontractors under art. 283-2 CGI. VAT refund claims may be suspended until documentary compliance is fully restored.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), the Republic's central bank and head of the French balance-of-payments reporting regime, acting within the Eurosystem/ECB framework; banking licensing and AML/CFT supervision are exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), while foreign-investment screening and economic-dossier review sit with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member and applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU. There is no exchange-control authorisation, no surrender obligation, and no restriction on holding or remitting dividends, loan repayments, royalties, or liquidation proceeds to non-resident shareholders of a French SAS. The operative constraints are documentary: cross-border financial flows equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 per transaction are declared monthly through the resident bank to the Banque de France, and non-EU investments must be pre-notified under Decree No. 2019-1590 where the target falls within a protected sector. A hyperscale datacenter mechanical-and-cooling EPC contractor sits outside the defence/security and critical-technology categories (subject to a case-by-case check where the scope includes cybersecurity, classified data processing, or critical infrastructure hosting), so pure construction activity requires no prior ministerial authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. The French and EU regimes impose no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to surrender export receipts. A French SAS may lawfully retain, convert, or disburse USD/CNY/EUR export and milestone proceeds in commercial bank accounts; the only duty is the Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration of cross-border settlements above EUR 12,500, filed by the bank on a monthly basis. This permits the EPC contractor to match USD-denominated capex procurement against USD-denominated receivables without forced conversion to EUR.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Primary operational account (compte courant) + project capital escrow account (compte séquestre)
Operational account + trade-finance settlement vault (documentary letters of credit and collections)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale / déclaration de résultats n°2065-SD with annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) - French State Tax Authority; filed via EDI/EFI online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months following fiscal year close; for a calendar year ending 31 December, filing is due by the 3rd working day after 1 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal demand and a 5% penalty on unpaid assessed tax, plus 0.2% monthly late interest; continued failure allows tax lien and administrative strike-off from the RCS after repeated years of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder approval of annual financial statements (approbation des comptes annuels à l'assemblée générale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minutes placed in the statutory minute book; subsequently attached to the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The shareholders' meeting must be convened within six months of the balance sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, approval must occur before 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain approval within six months allows any interested party to apply to the court for the date to be fixed, and the president of the court may order the appointment of a special auditor; recurrent failure supports judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual statutory financial statements and auditor's report (dépôt des comptes annuels) at the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce - French Companies Registry via guichet-entreprises.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the shareholders' meeting approval of accounts; absolute deadline is one month subsequent to the 30 June approval deadline for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 1,000 per day may be imposed; two consecutive years of non-deposit trigger the registry's administrative strike-off (radiation) and possible legal incapacity of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution return and payment (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises / déclaration n°1447-C)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax services under the DGFiP - French State Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration to be filed by 15 May of the levy year; principal payment due by 15 December of the levy year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration or non-declaration carries a 5% surcharge and 0.2% monthly late interest on unpaid amounts; continued failure may lead to tax enforcement measures and administrative penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (UBO) annual accuracy confirmation accompanying RCS annual filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce - French Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The declaration must be initially filed at incorporation, updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial owners, and confirmed as unchanged at each annual accounts deposit within the statutory filing window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the UBO declaration after a shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change is subject to registry correction orders and financial sanctions; persistent omission supports administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SAS if at the close of the financial year at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: total balance sheet above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeding fifty employees during the financial year. The audit may also be required by the articles of association, a shareholder resolution, or a court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles (French GAAP / Plan Comptable Général - PCG) apply to statutory financial statements; EU-IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The UBO register is filed at incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any direct or indirect shareholding change, voting-right change, or appointment of a legal beneficiary. At each annual deposit of financial statements, the entity must confirm that the previously filed UBO declaration remains accurate. Share transfers must be recorded in the share transfer register, and if the transfer changes beneficial ownership, a fresh UBO update must be submitted before the next RCS annual filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des actions et mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors (Registre des décisions sociales)
Minute Book (Registre des assemblées générales et procès-verbaux)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate (Article 219-I CGI); reduced 15% rate applies to the first €42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs meeting Article 44 sexies-0 A conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays for data-center EPC activities. Applicable incentives include: French research tax credit (CIR) 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100 million and 5% above; Innovation tax credit (CII) 20% of eligible innovation expenditure up to €400 thousand per year; young innovative company (JEI) status may provide temporary CIT exemption and payroll tax exemptions; carryback of losses limited to €1 million against prior-year profits is available. Effective rate may also be reduced by the 15% reduced CIT band and the use of accelerated depreciation for energy-efficient cooling and electrical infrastructure where compliant with L. 45-1 CGI.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no fixed-year limitation under French law); however, annual utilizsation is statutorily capped at €1 million plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding €1 million per fiscal year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa 2065-SD (Déclaration de Résultats) plus the full liasse fiscale schedules 2050-SD to 2059-SD, submitted electronically through the DGFiP online filing portal ('Téléprocédure Impot.gouv.fr' professional space). Non-resident entities with a French permanent establishment must file using the same portal and must establish an e-filing mandate with an EDI/EFI service provider.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year closing on 31 December, the return must be filed no later than the second working day following 1 May (generally 3 May, extended to the next business day when a holiday intervenes). For a fiscal year ending other than 31 December, the filing deadline is the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: SIREN, French APE/NAF code, legal form, registered address, fiscal year opening and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French registered office address of the SAS or the address of the permanent establishment. For a foreign-owned SAS, disclose the non-resident parent company and its tax residence jurisdiction in the associated French information fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting method and fiscal period confirmation: accrual accounting is mandatory; indicate whether the French entity is under French GAAP or, for consolidated groups, IFRS as allowed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the French SAS is a subsidiary of a non-resident EPC group, confirm that the fiscal period aligns with the French statutory year end; any off-calendar year-end must be approved administratively.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income or loss for the period: the before-tax result taken from the statutory profit-and-loss statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all transactions with non-resident affiliates are recorded under arm's length terms; accounting net income drives the tax base before reintegrations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after tax reintegrations and deductions, including transfer pricing adjustments, non-deductible charges, carried-forward losses and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify and separately schedule non-deductible cross-border amounts, off-market intercompany procurement margins, management fees, guarantee fees and engineering recharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses brought forward and deducted during the current year, including the computed annual utilisation cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses sustained by the French taxable entity (SAS or PE) are eligible; losses from a foreign head office cannot be transferred to the French branch unless a treaty permits branch-loss carryover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2054-SD – Fixed Assets and Depreciation Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fixed asset movements and depreciation charges for EPC-related electromechanical fixtures, cooling systems and data-center installations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For assets procured via non-resident group entities, capitalise the arm's length purchase price and support with import customs declarations and title transfer documents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% automatic surcharge on tax due if the return is filed within 30 days after the deadline; bad-faith inaccuracy: 40% surcharge; deliberate tax fraud: 80% surcharge. Interest is charged at 0.20% per month on unpaid tax from the statutory payment date. Failure to provide transfer-pricing documentation may trigger an additional penalty of 5% of the reassessed transferred profit, subject to a minimum of €10,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French SAS to a non-resident corporate beneficiary, the statutory withholding tax rate is 25% under Article 119-2 CGI. For non-resident individuals, a 30% flat withholding rate generally applies (including the 17.2% social levies on dividends treated as capital income). Mixed and treaty situations may reduce the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply an income tax treaty (DTA) relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide to the French paying entity: (i) a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority; (ii) a completed French Form 5000 (Certificate of Fiscal Residence) or the equivalent treaty residence attestation; and (iii) a beneficial-ownership statement. The French entity may reduce the dividend withholding rate at source if the DTA certificate is received before the distribution. If statutory withholding was imposed in the absence of prior documentation, the non-resident must file a claim on Form 5001/5033 with the French withholding tax office, attaching the TRC, dated dividend allocation, and proof of beneficial ownership. For EU-resident qualifying shareholders, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may allow a 0% withholding tax exemption if the conditions of Article 145/119 ter CGI are met, including a 5% participation held at least two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory French withholding tax on non-resident IP royalties is 33.33% (Article 182 B CGI); tax treaties commonly reduce the rate to 5–10%, subject to beneficial ownership and substance requirements. Interest: arm's length interest on ordinary commercial bank loans paid to non-resident lenders is generally exempt from French withholding tax; interest paid on certain shareholder current accounts or bond issuances may be exposed to withholding at 12–25% or to denial under Article 238A if paid toward a non-cooperative jurisdiction; most DTAs allocate interest taxing rights to the residence country or reduce the source withholding rate to 0–10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The mandatory Master File and Local File in France apply where the French entity, or the group to which it belongs, has annual turnover or balance-sheet total of at least €400 million (Article L.13 AA LPF); the Country-by-Country Report threshold is €750 million consolidated group turnover. Even below €400 million, a prudent SAS exposed to cross-border EPC procurement must prepare contemporaneous industry, functional and pricing evidence for audit defense.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the offshore sense, but the substance doctrine is embedded in the French abuse-of-law provision (Article L64 LPF), the OECD/IF principal-purpose test, and the EU ATAD general anti-abuse rule. For a French SAS engaged in hyperscale data-center electromechanical EPC, economic substance requires proper local board decisions, actual technical staff, project-management oversight, bank accounts and risk control in France. Absence of substance may invalidate treaty relief, cause the 80% abuse penalty, and trigger the recharacterisation of inter-company arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional suppression or false statement of taxable income, such as recording hyperscale data-center EPC revenues in offshore accounts, filing fictitious cost invoices, or destroying accounting books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI: up to 5 years' imprisonment and a €500,000 fine in aggravated cases; automatic 80% fraud surcharge; monthly 0.20% late-payment interest; exclusion from French public contracts; Corporate veil may be pierced to reach personal assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally direct or approve the concealment are criminally liable and may be sentenced to imprisonment, fined, stripped of management rights, subjected to travel bans, and ordered by the criminal court to pay civil restitution of the defrauded tax debt and penalties under Article L.267 LPF.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Transfer Pricing / Sham Intercompany Contracts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a shell buyer or regional engineering company in a low-tax jurisdiction without operational capability to inflate procurement costs or absorb EPC margins from the French SAS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax recharacterisation at arm's length and reassessment; 40% bad-faith penalty (or 80% for abuse of law); transfer-pricing documentation deficiency penalty of 5% of the reassessed transferred profit, minimum €10,000; denial of expense deduction when the arrangement lacks economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing fraudulent transfer-pricing declarations may face criminal prosecution for fraud, civil restoration of adjusted tax, and judicial disqualification; a French court may apply veil-piercing where the SAS is a mere conduit for the non-resident controller.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to declare the true beneficial owner in the French beneficial-owner register (RBE), maintaining bearer share arrangements, or interposing opaque entities to shield the controlling shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBE non-compliance is punishable by criminal fine up to €20,000 for the company and up to €10,000 per legal representative; concealment of beneficial ownership may be treated as money laundering; administrative penalty up to 80% of the tax due in the case of an artificial scheme; statutes require identifying the beneficial owner before payment of dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company officers are subject to criminal imprisonment for deliberate non-disclosure, personal monetary fines, travel bans prohibiting exit from French territory while under investigation, and civil liability for all tax and penalties resulting from the undisclosed ownership structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividend distributions through an intermediary entity in a favorable tax treaty solely to escape France's 25% or 30% withholding tax, without real business purpose or local employees/administration at the conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the DTA reduced rate or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption; statutory 25% withholding tax applied retroactively; abuse-of-law surcharge of 80%; no tax-refund availability; the intermediary is often ignored for French tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly execute treaty-shopping structures can be prosecuted for aggravated tax fraud, personally ordered to pay withholding tax and 80% penalties, subjected to travel bans during proceedings, and, in severe criminal cases, sentenced to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Omission of Transfer-Pricing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual liasse fiscale by the statutory deadline or failure to produce the required Master File and Local File within 30 days of a formal French tax-verification request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% late-filing surcharge; 40% penalty for inaccurate returns; 0.20% monthly interest on unpaid CIT; if documentation is missing, 5% of the reassessed transferred profit with a minimum €10,000 penalty; potential tax base estimation by the tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where non-filing is deliberate concealment, directors may be criminally prosecuted for tax evasion; the DGFiP may invoke individual liability for the company's tax debt if the director committed a serious anomaly in the management of the company and caused its insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making payments of engineering fees, royalties, interest or procurement invoice settlements to a bank account held in a jurisdiction listed as non-cooperative (ETNC), without demonstration of real counterparty business and beneficial owner disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory tax disallowance of the expense; 33.33% or higher withholding on royalties and certain interest payments (up to 75% in some ETNC cases); 80% penalty for abusive offshore arrangements; unreported ETNC payments create a presumption of fiscal concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct such payments may be prosecuted for fraudulent management and tax evasion, subjected to civil compensation to the French treasury, travel bans, judicial control, and imprisonment of up to five years; courts may order freezing of personal bank accounts and passport surrender.
